findings.title: 3 subscription lifecycle events not delivered
evidence: Not delivered to any enabled endpoint: customer.subscription.updated, customer.subscription.deleted, invoice.payment_failed.
findings.why: A subscription business learns about renewals, failures and cancellations through these events. If one is not delivered to anything, your records and the customer's access stop matching what Stripe bills.
findings.fix: Add the missing events to an enabled endpoint (or use all events), and make the handler idempotent on the event id. Handle checkout.session.completed to provision, invoice.paid to extend access, invoice.payment_failed to start recovery, customer.subscription.updated and customer.subscription.deleted to change or end access.

findings.title: 1 endpoint on plain HTTP
findings.why: Event payloads carry billing data and travel in clear over HTTP, and the request cannot be trusted to come from where it claims. Stripe requires HTTPS for live-mode endpoints.
findings.fix: Serve the endpoint over HTTPS with a valid certificate and update the endpoint URL. Keep verifying the Stripe-Signature header regardless of the transport.

findings.title: 1 subscription failing for 7+ days
evidence: past_due: 1 subscription, oldest since 2026-09-21 (35 days): sub_1PastD….
Threshold: 7 days, counted from the oldest open invoice of the subscription, or from the start of its current period when no open invoice was listed (so a lower bound).
findings.why: A subscription that stays in a failing state is revenue you are owed and have not collected, and usually a customer who still has, or has silently lost, access. The longer it lasts the less likely it is recovered.
findings.fix: Decide the end state of failed payments (Dashboard, Billing, Revenue recovery: cancel, mark unpaid or leave past due), contact the customers with the oldest failures, and make the application treat past_due and unpaid explicitly instead of as active. The Billing portal link lets a customer update the card themselves.

findings.title: 1 subscription with no payment method on file, set to charge automatically
evidence: Neither the subscription nor its customer has a default payment method or source.
findings.why: A subscription set to charge automatically with no default payment method on the subscription or the customer will fail its next renewal. It becomes past_due, costs a failed-payment cycle and often a customer.
findings.fix: Ask these customers to add a payment method (the Billing portal's update-payment-method link works), or switch the subscription to send_invoice if invoicing is intended. Collect the payment method at checkout with setup_future_usage or a Checkout subscription session so it is saved as the default.

findings.title: 1 trial ending within 7 days with no payment method
evidence: Behaviour when the trial ends without a payment method: create_invoice.
findings.why: When a trial ends with no payment method the first invoice cannot be paid: the customer is cancelled, paused or left past due, depending on the trial settings, at the moment they have just decided to stay.
findings.fix: Collect a payment method before the trial ends (Checkout with payment_method_collection=always, or a reminder email from the customer.subscription.trial_will_end event, sent three days before). Set trial_settings.end_behavior.missing_payment_method deliberately: cancel or pause rather than create_invoice.

findings.title: 1 subscription without automatic tax
evidence: 1 active tax registration, and 1 of 5 billing subscriptions have automatic tax off: sub_1Untax….
findings.why: You are registered to collect tax, but these subscriptions are billed without calculating it. The tax is then either not collected, which you owe anyway, or collected by hand and inconsistently.
findings.fix: Enable automatic tax on the subscriptions (automatic_tax[enabled]=true on new ones, and update existing ones), set a tax behavior on the prices, and make sure customers have a valid address. Review the invoices already issued with your accountant.

findings.title: Automatic tax is on but tax settings are not active
evidence: 4 subscriptions use automatic tax: sub_1PastD…, sub_1Trial…, sub_1Leavi…, sub_1AbCdE….
Tax settings status: pending; missing: head_office.address.
findings.why: Automatic tax cannot calculate anything until the head office address and tax settings are complete. Invoices and checkouts then fail to compute tax or fall back to no tax.
findings.fix: Complete the missing tax settings (Dashboard, Tax, Settings) and check that Stripe Tax shows the status as active.

findings.title: 1 webhook endpoint disabled
findings.why: Stripe disables an endpoint that keeps failing, and a disabled endpoint silently stops receiving events. It is also a sign that someone's handler was broken for days.
findings.fix: Find out why deliveries failed (Dashboard, Webhooks, the endpoint's event deliveries), fix the handler, then re-enable the endpoint or delete it if it is obsolete. Replay the missed events from the dashboard or reconcile against the API.

findings.title: API version differs from the account's on 1 endpoint
findings.why: The payload of an event follows the API version of its endpoint. If the endpoint and the account differ, the shape your handler receives differs from what the rest of your code reads from the API, and an account upgrade changes only one of them.
findings.fix: Choose one version on purpose: set the endpoint's version to the one your handler was written against, or upgrade handler and account together. Test the handler against payloads of the target version before switching.

findings.title: 1 invoice open for 14+ days
evidence: Oldest reference date: 2026-09-21 (35 days), counted from the due date, or the creation date when there is none.
findings.why: An open invoice that nobody pays and nothing closes is revenue that is neither collected nor written off. It keeps the customer past due, inflates receivables and hides failed payment flows.
findings.fix: Follow up with the customer (the hosted invoice page has a pay button), retry or collect the payment, or void or mark the invoice uncollectible if it will not be paid. Add an alert for invoices open longer than your collection policy.

findings.title: 1 invoice open with no retry left
evidence: in_1Exhau…; 4 attempts each, no next attempt scheduled.
findings.why: An invoice that was attempted, has no next attempt scheduled and is still open is out of retries and out of sight: Stripe will not try again and nothing else is going to collect it.
findings.fix: Review the retry settings (Dashboard, Billing, Revenue recovery). Choose what happens when the last retry fails (cancel the subscription, mark it unpaid or leave it past due), and contact the customer or collect manually for these invoices.

findings.title: No active Billing portal configuration
findings.why: Without the Billing portal customers cannot update a card, download invoices or cancel on their own. Every one of those becomes a support ticket, and a failed card that the customer cannot fix is lost revenue.
findings.fix: Save a portal configuration (Dashboard, Settings, Billing, Customer portal) with payment method updates, invoice history and cancellation enabled, then create portal sessions from your account page and from failed-payment emails.

findings.title: 1 active price with no tax behavior
evidence: The tax settings define no default tax behavior.
findings.why: A price with no tax behavior leaves it to chance whether the displayed amount includes tax. With automatic tax the calculation can fail, and customers are charged a total they did not expect.
findings.fix: Set tax_behavior to inclusive or exclusive on each price (prices are immutable in most fields, so create a replacement price and archive the old one), or set a default tax behavior in the tax settings.

findings.title: Pending cancellations have no self-service way back
evidence: 1 subscription set to cancel at period end: sub_1Leavi….
No active Billing portal configuration has cancellation enabled, so customers cannot undo a pending cancellation there.
findings.why: A customer who has scheduled a cancellation is the cheapest customer to keep. Without a way to undo it themselves, and without the reason they leave, there is nothing to win them back with before the period ends.
findings.fix: Enable cancellation in the Billing portal configuration (customers then see an option to keep their subscription while a cancellation is pending), turn on cancellation reasons, and send a win-back message from the customer.subscription.updated event while cancel_at_period_end is true. The API cannot show whether such a message exists; see --checklist.

findings.title: 1 active product with no tax code
evidence: prod_1AbCdE…; the tax settings define no default tax code.
findings.why: Tax rates depend on what is sold. A product without a tax code is taxed with the account's default code, which is wrong for software, services and digital goods that have their own treatment.
findings.fix: Set the right tax code on each product (Dashboard, Product catalog) or set a sensible default tax code in the tax settings.

findings.title: 2 currencies in use
findings.why: Several currencies multiply the reporting, tax and reconciliation work, expose you to exchange-rate swings on settlement and make revenue figures hard to compare. It is sometimes deliberate, so this is for review, not a defect.
findings.fix: Confirm that each currency is intended. If not, archive the prices in the stray currency and move the subscriptions. If it is, make sure your reporting, tax settings and payouts handle each currency.
